name: CompTIA Network+
summary: Networking concepts, implementation, operations, security and troubleshooting.

domains.name: Networking Concepts
domains.summary: How networks work: models, protocols, addressing and topologies.
topics: Modern environments: SDN, SD-WAN, IaC, zero trust

domains.name: Network Implementation
domains.summary: Build and configure routing, switching and wireless networks.
topics: Switching: VLANs, trunking, STP, link aggregation

domains.name: Network Operations
domains.summary: Keep networks documented, monitored, resilient and well-run.
topics: Network monitoring: SNMP, flow data, logs
IPv4/IPv6 network services: DHCP, DNS, NTP
Access and management methods: VPN, SSH, console, jump box

domains.name: Network Security
domains.summary: Secure network infrastructure and defend against attacks.
topics: Security concepts: CIA, PKI, IAM, encryption
Network security features and defence techniques

domains.name: Network Troubleshooting
domains.summary: Troubleshoot network problems methodically with the right tools.
topics: Tools and protocols: ping, traceroute, nslookup, packet capture

questions.prompt: At which OSI layer do routers primarily operate?
questions.explanation: Routers forward packets using IP addresses at Layer 3 (Network).

questions.prompt: Which protocol is connectionless?
questions.explanation: UDP sends datagrams without a handshake or delivery guarantees.

questions.prompt: How many usable host addresses are in a /26 subnet?
questions.explanation: A /26 has 64 addresses; minus network and broadcast leaves 62 usable hosts.

questions.prompt: Which address is a private IPv4 address?
What is the IPv6 equivalent of 127.0.0.1?
questions.explanation: ::1 is the IPv6 loopback address.

questions.prompt: Which port does SSH use?
questions.explanation: SSH uses TCP 22; Telnet uses 23.

questions.prompt: Which cloud deployment model is shared by several organizations with common needs?
questions.explanation: A community cloud serves multiple organizations with shared requirements.

questions.prompt: Which device separates broadcast domains?
questions.explanation: Routers (and VLANs on Layer 3 switches) separate broadcast domains.

questions.prompt: Which protocol prevents switching loops in a Layer 2 network?
questions.explanation: Spanning Tree Protocol blocks redundant paths to prevent loops.

questions.prompt: A switch port must carry traffic for several VLANs to another switch. How should it be configured?
questions.explanation: Trunk ports tag frames with 802.1Q so multiple VLANs share one link.

questions.prompt: Which routing protocol is a link-state protocol commonly used inside an organization?
questions.explanation: OSPF is an open link-state interior gateway protocol.

questions.prompt: Which routing protocol is used between ISPs on the internet?
questions.explanation: BGP is the exterior gateway protocol that routes between autonomous systems.

questions.prompt: Which Wi-Fi band offers the most non-overlapping channels?
questions.explanation: 6 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E/7) adds many wide, non-overlapping channels.

questions.prompt: Which protocol collects performance data from network devices using MIBs?
questions.explanation: SNMP polls and receives traps from devices defined in MIBs.

questions.prompt: What does an SLA define?
questions.explanation: A Service Level Agreement defines expected performance such as uptime and response times.

questions.prompt: Which metric measures the average time to repair a failed device?
questions.explanation: MTTR is mean time to repair. MTBF measures reliability between failures.

questions.prompt: Which site type has power and connectivity but no equipment ready?
questions.explanation: A cold site is an empty facility; hot sites are fully equipped and ready.

questions.prompt: Which attack floods a switch's MAC table so it acts like a hub?
questions.explanation: MAC flooding overflows the CAM table, forcing the switch to flood frames out all ports.

questions.prompt: Which feature restricts a switch port to specific MAC addresses?
questions.explanation: Port security limits or locks the MAC addresses allowed on a port.

questions.prompt: Which VPN type connects two office networks permanently?
questions.explanation: Site-to-site VPNs link entire networks through gateway devices.

questions.prompt: A security model that verifies every request regardless of network location is called:
questions.explanation: Zero trust assumes no implicit trust based on location; every access is verified.

questions.prompt: Users on one VLAN can't reach the internet but others can. The FIRST thing to check is:
choices: That VLAN's default gateway / DHCP scope
questions.explanation: Since other VLANs work, the problem is local to that VLAN's gateway or DHCP configuration.

questions.prompt: Which command shows the path packets take to a destination on Windows?
questions.explanation: tracert (traceroute on Linux/macOS) lists each hop.

questions.prompt: A long copper run shows signal loss over distance. This is called:
questions.explanation: Attenuation is signal weakening over distance; Cat6 Ethernet is limited to 100 m.

questions.prompt: Voice calls sound choppy even though bandwidth is sufficient. Which metric is MOST likely high?
questions.explanation: Jitter is variation in packet delay and badly affects real-time traffic like VoIP.

questions.prompt: Which tool would you use to find where a cable run terminates in a patch panel?
questions.explanation: A toner and probe traces a cable by sending a tone down it.

questions.prompt: Which OSI layer handles data formatting, character encoding and encryption so applications can understand each other's data?
questions.explanation: The Presentation layer (Layer 6) translates, encrypts and compresses data into a form the Application layer can use.

questions.prompt: Which OSI layer is responsible for setting up, maintaining and tearing down dialogs between two applications?
questions.explanation: The Session layer (Layer 5) manages dialog control, checkpoints and termination of communication sessions.

questions.prompt: What is the protocol data unit (PDU) called at the Data Link layer?
questions.explanation: Layer 2 encapsulates packets into frames by adding a header with MAC addresses and a trailer containing the FCS.

questions.prompt: A TCP header has just been added to application data. What is the resulting PDU called?
questions.explanation: At the Transport layer, TCP data units are called segments (UDP units are often called datagrams).

questions.prompt: How many usable host addresses does a /28 subnet provide?
questions.explanation: A /28 leaves 4 host bits: 2^4 = 16 addresses, minus the network and broadcast addresses, gives 14 usable hosts.

questions.prompt: Which dotted-decimal subnet mask corresponds to a /21 prefix?
questions.explanation: A /21 sets 8+8+5 bits; five bits in the third octet equal 128+64+32+16+8 = 248, giving 255.255.248.0.

questions.prompt: What is the broadcast address of the subnet containing host 192.168.10.77/27?
questions.explanation: A /27 uses blocks of 32, so .77 falls in the .64–.95 subnet, whose broadcast address is 192.168.10.95.

questions.prompt: What is the network address of host 172.16.45.200 with a /20 mask?
questions.explanation: A /20 uses blocks of 16 in the third octet; 45 falls in the 32–47 block, so the network is 172.16.32.0.

questions.prompt: A department needs 50 host addresses. Which prefix length wastes the fewest addresses while still fitting?
questions.explanation: A /26 provides 62 usable hosts; a /27 offers only 30, and a /25 (126 hosts) wastes more space.

questions.prompt: Which prefix length can be used on point-to-point links under RFC 3021 because no network or broadcast address is needed?
questions.explanation: RFC 3021 allows /31 masks on point-to-point links, using both addresses for the two endpoints.

questions.prompt: If 10.0.0.0/8 is divided into /16 subnets, how many subnets result?
questions.explanation: Borrowing 8 bits (from /8 to /16) yields 2^8 = 256 subnets.

questions.prompt: A host configured for DHCP shows an address of 169.254.33.10. What type of address is this?
questions.explanation: Addresses in 169.254.0.0/16 are assigned by APIPA when a client cannot reach a DHCP server.

questions.prompt: What is the 100.64.0.0/10 address block reserved for?
choices: Shared address space for carrier-grade NAT
questions.explanation: RFC 6598 reserves 100.64.0.0/10 for ISPs to use between their CGNAT devices and customer equipment.

questions.prompt: Which IPv4 range is used for multicast (formerly Class D)?
questions.explanation: Class D addresses from 224.0.0.0 through 239.255.255.255 are reserved for multicast groups.

questions.prompt: Every IPv6-enabled interface automatically has an address from which prefix for local-segment communication?
questions.explanation: Link-local addresses come from fe80::/10 and are created automatically on every IPv6 interface.

questions.prompt: Which IPv6 address range is most similar in purpose to IPv4 RFC 1918 private addresses?
questions.explanation: Unique local addresses are routable within an organization but not on the internet, like RFC 1918 space.

questions.prompt: What is the correctly shortened form of 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:ff00:0042:8329?
questions.explanation: Leading zeros in each hextet are dropped and one run of all-zero hextets is replaced by a single '::'.

questions.prompt: Which IPv6 function replaces ARP for resolving neighbors' link-layer addresses?
questions.explanation: NDP uses ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicitation and Neighbor Advertisement messages to resolve link-layer addresses.

questions.prompt: When an IPv6 host builds a modified EUI-64 interface ID from its MAC address, what does it do?
choices: Inserts FFFE in the middle of the MAC and flips the seventh bit
Appends 0000 to the end of the MAC
Copies the MAC twice to fill 64 bits
Hashes the MAC with the router's prefix
questions.explanation: Modified EUI-64 splits the 48-bit MAC, inserts FFFE in the middle, and inverts the universal/local bit.

questions.prompt: A network runs IPv4 and IPv6 at the same time on the same interfaces and devices. What is this transition approach called?
questions.explanation: Dual stack configures both protocol stacks on devices so each can be used natively.

questions.prompt: What does NAT64 allow?
choices: Two IPv6 networks to share one global prefix
IPv6-only clients to communicate with IPv4-only servers
IPv6 hosts to obtain addresses without a router
IPv4 packets to be carried inside IPv6 tunnels
questions.explanation: NAT64, usually paired with DNS64, translates between IPv6 and IPv4 so IPv6-only hosts can reach IPv4 resources.

questions.prompt: Which TCP port does LDAP over TLS (LDAPS) use by default?
questions.explanation: LDAPS listens on TCP 636, while unencrypted LDAP uses 389.

questions.prompt: A Windows file share is accessed directly over TCP without NetBIOS. Which port does SMB use?
questions.explanation: Modern SMB runs directly over TCP port 445.

questions.prompt: A firewall rule must allow remote desktop sessions to Windows servers. Which port should be opened?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) uses TCP/UDP 3389 by default.

questions.prompt: Which port does Microsoft SQL Server listen on by default?
questions.explanation: Microsoft SQL Server uses TCP 1433; 3306 is MySQL, 1521 is Oracle and 5432 is PostgreSQL.

questions.prompt: Which protocol and port does Network Time Protocol use?
questions.explanation: NTP synchronizes clocks using UDP port 123.

questions.prompt: Which port do network devices typically send SNMP trap messages to?
questions.explanation: Managers listen for unsolicited traps on UDP 162; polling requests go to agents on UDP 161.

questions.prompt: A mail client retrieves messages over an encrypted IMAP connection. Which port is used?
questions.explanation: IMAP over TLS (IMAPS) uses port 993; 995 is POP3S and 143 is plain IMAP.

questions.prompt: Which ports are typically used by Session Initiation Protocol for VoIP signaling?
questions.explanation: SIP uses 5060 for unencrypted signaling and 5061 for SIP over TLS.

questions.prompt: Which file-transfer protocol uses UDP port 69 and provides no authentication?
questions.explanation: Trivial FTP runs over UDP 69 with no login, which is why it is used for simple tasks like booting or loading firmware.

questions.prompt: In which situation does DNS use TCP port 53 rather than UDP?
questions.explanation: Zone transfers (AXFR/IXFR) and large responses use TCP 53, while most ordinary queries use UDP.

questions.prompt: Which IP protocol number is used by Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE)?
questions.explanation: GRE is IP protocol 47; ESP is 50, AH is 51 and OSPF is 89.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of the TCP three-way handshake?
questions.explanation: The client sends SYN, the server replies with SYN-ACK, and the client confirms with ACK.

questions.prompt: Which TCP flag immediately aborts a connection rather than closing it gracefully?
questions.explanation: RST resets a connection abruptly, whereas FIN starts the graceful four-way close.

questions.prompt: A public DNS provider advertises the same IP address from dozens of data centers so users reach the closest one. What is this addressing method?
questions.explanation: Anycast assigns one address to many nodes, and routing delivers traffic to the nearest one.

questions.prompt: In which cloud service model does the customer manage the operating system and applications while the provider manages the physical hardware?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as a Service gives customers virtual machines, storage and networks, leaving the OS and above to them.

questions.prompt: Developers want to deploy code to a managed runtime without patching or maintaining the operating system. Which cloud model fits?
questions.explanation: Platform as a Service provides a managed runtime so developers only manage their applications and data.

questions.prompt: Which cloud characteristic describes resources being automatically added or removed as demand rises and falls?
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the dynamic, automatic provisioning and release of resources to match workload.

questions.prompt: In a cloud VPC, instances in a private subnet need outbound internet access for updates but must not accept inbound connections from the internet. What should be used?
choices: A public elastic IP on each instance
An internet gateway attached directly to the subnet
questions.explanation: A NAT gateway lets private instances start outbound connections while blocking unsolicited inbound traffic.

questions.prompt: How do cloud security groups typically differ from network ACLs?
choices: Security groups are stateless and applied at the subnet level
Security groups only apply to outbound traffic
Security groups are stateful and applied at the instance level
Security groups only filter by MAC address
questions.explanation: Security groups track connection state and attach to instances; NACLs are usually stateless and apply to subnets.

questions.prompt: In software-defined networking, which plane is centralized in the SDN controller?
questions.explanation: SDN separates the control plane into a central controller that programs forwarding on the data-plane devices.

questions.prompt: In an SDN architecture, what does the northbound API connect?
choices: Two controllers in different data centers
The controller to switches and routers
The controller to applications and orchestration tools
questions.explanation: Northbound APIs expose the controller to applications; southbound APIs connect it to network devices.

questions.prompt: How large is the VXLAN Network Identifier, allowing far more segments than 802.1Q VLANs?
questions.explanation: The 24-bit VNI supports about 16 million segments, versus 4,094 usable VLANs with a 12-bit VLAN ID.

questions.prompt: In a spine-and-leaf data center design, how are the switches connected?
choices: Every spine connects to one leaf in a ring
Spines connect to a single core router through each leaf
Every leaf connects to every spine, and leaves do not connect to each other
Leaves connect to each other in a full mesh with no spines
questions.explanation: Each leaf uplinks to every spine, so any two servers are a predictable number of hops apart.

questions.prompt: How many links are needed to connect six sites in a full mesh?
questions.explanation: A full mesh needs n(n-1)/2 links: 6 x 5 / 2 = 15.

questions.prompt: Which DHCP message sequence correctly describes a client obtaining an address?
questions.explanation: DHCP uses the DORA exchange: Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge.

questions.prompt: A router learns a route to the same prefix from both OSPF and internal EIGRP. Using default administrative distances, which route is installed?
choices: The OSPF route, because link-state protocols are always preferred
The EIGRP route, because its AD of 90 is lower than OSPF's 110
The route with the higher metric
questions.explanation: Routers prefer the source with the lowest administrative distance; internal EIGRP (90) beats OSPF (110).

questions.prompt: A routing table has 10.0.0.0/8, 10.1.0.0/16 and 10.1.1.0/24. Which route is used for a packet to 10.1.1.5?
questions.explanation: Routers choose the longest prefix match, and /24 is the most specific route containing 10.1.1.5.

questions.prompt: Which notation represents an IPv4 default route?
questions.explanation: 0.0.0.0/0 matches every destination and is used when no more specific route exists.

questions.prompt: An administrator adds a static route with an administrative distance of 200 as a backup to an OSPF-learned route. What is this called?
questions.explanation: A floating static route has a higher AD than the primary route and only enters the table if that route disappears.

questions.prompt: In a multi-area OSPF design, which area must all other areas connect to?
questions.explanation: Area 0 is the OSPF backbone, and all other areas must attach to it, either directly or through a virtual link.

questions.prompt: Which TCP port does BGP use to form peering sessions?
questions.explanation: BGP neighbors establish sessions over TCP 179.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum hop count RIP allows before a destination is considered unreachable?
questions.explanation: RIP allows up to 15 hops; a metric of 16 means the route is unreachable.

questions.prompt: Which open-standard first-hop redundancy protocol lets two routers share a virtual default gateway address?
questions.explanation: VRRP is an IETF standard FHRP; HSRP and GLBP are Cisco proprietary, and LACP is for link aggregation.

questions.prompt: Two switches are connected by four physical links that should act as one logical link with negotiation. Which protocol should be used?
questions.explanation: LACP negotiates and bundles multiple physical links into a single logical port channel.

questions.prompt: On an 802.1Q trunk, how is traffic for the native VLAN handled by default?
questions.explanation: 802.1Q sends native VLAN frames without a tag, so both ends must agree on the native VLAN.

questions.prompt: How many bytes does an 802.1Q tag add to an Ethernet frame?
questions.explanation: The 802.1Q tag is 4 bytes: a 2-byte TPID and a 2-byte tag control field containing the 12-bit VLAN ID.

questions.prompt: An IP phone and a PC share one switch port. What is the usual way to keep voice traffic separate?
choices: Use port mirroring to copy voice traffic to a second port
Configure a voice VLAN on the access port alongside the data VLAN
Configure the port as a full trunk carrying all VLANs
Put the phone and PC in the same VLAN with QoS disabled
questions.explanation: A voice VLAN lets the phone tag its traffic separately while the PC uses the untagged data VLAN.

questions.prompt: How is the STP root bridge elected?
choices: The switch with the highest bridge ID
The switch with the most ports
The switch with the lowest bridge ID (priority plus MAC address)
questions.explanation: STP elects the switch with the lowest bridge ID; priority is compared first, then the MAC address.

questions.prompt: Which STP feature moves an access port connected to a workstation straight to forwarding, skipping the listening and learning states?
questions.explanation: PortFast sends edge ports directly to forwarding so end hosts get connectivity immediately.

questions.prompt: Which IEEE standard defines Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol?
questions.explanation: 802.1w defines RSTP, which converges much faster than the original 802.1D STP.

questions.prompt: An iSCSI storage network would perform better if each Ethernet frame carried more data. What should be configured?
choices: Jumbo frames with an MTU around 9000 bytes
questions.explanation: Jumbo frames reduce per-frame overhead for large transfers, which helps storage traffic.

questions.prompt: A new access point needs about 25 W from the switch. Which is the minimum PoE standard that can supply it?
questions.explanation: PoE+ (802.3at) provides up to 30 W at the switch port, while 802.3af provides only 15.4 W.

questions.prompt: In North America, which set of 2.4 GHz channels does not overlap?
questions.explanation: With 20 MHz channels at 5 MHz spacing, channels 1, 6 and 11 are the standard non-overlapping set.

questions.prompt: What does Wi-Fi 6E add compared with Wi-Fi 6?
choices: A maximum of 20 MHz channel widths
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi 6E extends 802.11ax into the 6 GHz band, adding much more spectrum.

questions.prompt: What is a drawback of using 80 MHz channel bonding in a dense 5 GHz deployment?
choices: Clients can no longer use WPA3
Fewer non-overlapping channels are available, raising co-channel interference
The AP must switch to the 2.4 GHz band
Range doubles and causes roaming failures
questions.explanation: Wider channels increase throughput per client but reduce the number of separate channels for neighboring APs.

questions.prompt: Two buildings 500 meters apart need a wireless point-to-point bridge. Which antenna type is most appropriate?
choices: Directional (such as a Yagi or parabolic dish)
Patch antenna mounted on an interior ceiling
questions.explanation: Directional antennas focus energy in one direction, giving the gain needed for long point-to-point links.

questions.prompt: Several APs broadcast the same SSID on the same network so clients can roam between them. What is this set of APs called?
questions.explanation: An ESS is several BSSs sharing one SSID, connected by a distribution system so clients can roam.

questions.prompt: Which wireless feature encourages dual-band clients to connect on 5 GHz rather than 2.4 GHz?
questions.explanation: Band steering pushes capable clients toward the less congested 5 GHz (or 6 GHz) band.

questions.prompt: Lightweight APs are managed centrally by a wireless LAN controller. Which protocol commonly tunnels their control and data traffic to the controller?
questions.explanation: CAPWAP is the standard protocol that lightweight APs use to communicate with a WLAN controller.

questions.prompt: Network cable must run through the air-handling space above a drop ceiling. What type of cable jacket is required?
questions.explanation: Plenum-rated jackets resist fire and produce less toxic smoke, which fire codes require in air-handling spaces.

questions.prompt: How is a traditional Ethernet crossover cable wired?
choices: Pins 1 and 8 swapped on one end only
T568A on one end and T568B on the other
questions.explanation: Using T568A on one end and T568B on the other swaps the transmit and receive pairs.

questions.prompt: Which tool seats twisted-pair conductors into a 110 block or keystone jack?
questions.explanation: A punch-down tool pushes each wire into an insulation-displacement contact and trims the excess.

questions.prompt: How tall is one rack unit (1U)?
questions.explanation: A rack unit is 1.75 inches; 19 inches is the standard rack width.

questions.prompt: In a hot aisle/cold aisle data center layout, how should servers be oriented?
choices: Intakes and exhausts alternate within each row
Exhausts face the cold aisle to warm incoming air
Server intakes face the cold aisle and exhausts face the hot aisle
All servers face the same direction across every row
questions.explanation: Facing rows front-to-front and back-to-back keeps cool intake air separate from hot exhaust air.

questions.prompt: Hosts in VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 must communicate through a multilayer switch. What should be configured on the switch?
choices: STP root bridge priority on both VLANs
A single access port shared by both VLANs
A switched virtual interface (SVI) for each VLAN with IP routing enabled
questions.explanation: SVIs act as the Layer 3 gateways for each VLAN, letting the multilayer switch route between them.

questions.prompt: A router with one physical interface routes between several VLANs over a trunk link. What does this design require?
choices: A separate DHCP server per VLAN on the router
Subinterfaces, each tagged with a VLAN ID and given a gateway IP
questions.explanation: Router-on-a-stick uses 802.1Q subinterfaces so one physical link can serve as the gateway for several VLANs.

questions.prompt: Clients on a new VLAN cannot get DHCP addresses because the DHCP server is on another subnet. What should be configured on the VLAN's router interface?
choices: A static ARP entry for the server
A DHCP relay (IP helper) address pointing to the server
questions.explanation: A DHCP relay forwards client broadcasts as unicasts to a DHCP server on another subnet.

questions.prompt: An office of 200 users shares one public IPv4 address, with sessions told apart by source port. What is this called?
choices: Dynamic NAT with an address pool
questions.explanation: PAT (NAT overload) maps many private addresses to one public address using unique port numbers.

questions.prompt: An internal web server must always appear on the internet at the same public IP address. Which NAT type is required?
questions.explanation: Static NAT maps one private address permanently to one public address, allowing inbound connections.

questions.prompt: A security team needs a copy of all traffic on a switch's uplink sent to their analyzer. What should be configured?
questions.explanation: Port mirroring copies frames from source ports or VLANs to a monitoring port for analysis.

questions.prompt: Which device spreads incoming client requests across a pool of web servers and removes servers that fail health checks?
questions.explanation: Load balancers distribute sessions across healthy back-end servers to improve performance and availability.

questions.prompt: Which transceiver should be used for a 10 Gbps link over multimode fiber within a building?
questions.explanation: 10GBASE-SR uses 850 nm light over multimode fiber; LR and ER are for single-mode fiber.

questions.prompt: Only a single fiber strand is available between two switches. Which transceiver type allows a full-duplex link?
choices: A media converter on one end only
BiDi transceivers using different wavelengths in each direction
questions.explanation: Bidirectional optics transmit and receive on different wavelengths over one strand, used as a matched pair.

questions.prompt: Which WAN technology forwards packets based on labels rather than IP lookups at each hop?
questions.explanation: MPLS routers switch traffic by short labels, which supports traffic engineering and provider VPN services.

questions.prompt: A company wants to send branch traffic over several broadband and LTE links, steering applications by measured link quality. What should it deploy?
questions.explanation: SD-WAN centrally manages multiple transport links and picks paths by application policy and real-time performance.

questions.prompt: Which feature does SNMPv3 add that SNMPv1 and v2c lack?
questions.explanation: SNMPv3 adds user-based authentication and encryption; earlier versions rely on plaintext community strings.

questions.prompt: In SNMP, what uniquely identifies a specific value such as an interface's input byte counter?
questions.explanation: Each managed object in a MIB has a unique OID, which managers use to query its value.

questions.prompt: A manager needs to know who is talking to whom, on which ports and how much, without capturing full packets. What should it collect?
choices: Flow data such as NetFlow or IPFIX
Full packet captures on every port
questions.explanation: Flow records summarize conversations (addresses, ports, byte counts) without storing payloads.

questions.prompt: Which syslog severity level is the most critical?
questions.explanation: Syslog severities run from 0 (Emergency, system unusable) to 7 (Debug).

questions.prompt: A network team records normal utilization, latency and error rates over several weeks to compare against future readings. What are they creating?
questions.explanation: A baseline captures normal behavior so anomalies and trends can be spotted later.

questions.prompt: Which system collects logs from firewalls, servers and switches, correlates events and raises alerts?
questions.explanation: A SIEM aggregates and correlates log data from many sources to detect and alert on security events.

questions.prompt: What does a recovery point objective (RPO) of four hours mean?
choices: Failover must be tested every four hours
Systems must be restored within four hours
No more than four hours of data may be lost after an incident
Backups must take less than four hours
questions.explanation: RPO is the maximum tolerable data loss measured in time, which drives backup frequency.

questions.prompt: Which metric states the maximum time allowed to restore a service after an outage?
questions.explanation: RTO is the target time to bring a service back to operation after a disruption.

questions.prompt: Which metric describes the average operating time between failures of a repairable component?
questions.explanation: Mean time between failures measures reliability as the average time a repairable device runs between failures.

questions.prompt: A DR site has hardware and network links in place but needs recent backups restored before it can take over. What type of site is this?
questions.explanation: A warm site has equipment ready but needs data restored and some setup, so it sits between hot and cold sites.

questions.prompt: Which recovery site keeps systems running with near-real-time data so failover takes minutes?
questions.explanation: A hot site is a fully equipped, continuously updated copy of production that can take over almost at once.

questions.prompt: Full backups run Sunday and differential backups run every other night. A failure occurs Thursday morning. What is needed to restore?
choices: Sunday's full backup and every differential since Sunday
Sunday's full backup and Wednesday's differential
Every backup from the past week in reverse order
questions.explanation: Each differential holds all changes since the last full backup, so only the full and the latest differential are needed.

questions.prompt: Full backups run Sunday and incremental backups run every other night. What is needed to restore after a failure on Thursday morning?
choices: Sunday's full backup plus the Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday incrementals
Sunday's full backup and Wednesday's incremental only
questions.explanation: Incrementals hold only changes since the previous backup, so the full and every later incremental must be restored in order.

questions.prompt: Two firewalls both process traffic at the same time, sharing the load, and either can carry everything if the other fails. What is this configuration?
questions.explanation: In active-active clusters all members handle traffic at once and absorb the load if a peer fails.

questions.prompt: Staff talk through their responses to a simulated ransomware outage in a meeting room without touching any systems. What is this?
questions.explanation: A tabletop exercise is a discussion-based walkthrough of the DR or incident plan without live changes.

questions.prompt: Before a core switch upgrade is approved by the change advisory board, which item should the change request include?
choices: A list of all user passwords
A rollback plan in case the change fails
questions.explanation: Change management requires documented back-out steps so the network can be restored if the change causes problems.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows IP subnets, VLANs and routing relationships rather than cable paths and rack locations?
questions.explanation: Logical diagrams show how traffic flows and how addressing is organized, independent of physical layout.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to see which devices sit in each rack position and how many units are free. Which document helps most?
questions.explanation: A rack diagram (elevation) shows each device's U position, along with power and free space.

questions.prompt: A vendor announces that a switch model will no longer receive security patches after a certain date. What lifecycle milestone is this?
questions.explanation: End of support means no more updates or patches, a key trigger for replacement planning.

questions.prompt: Which tool tracks subnet allocations, DHCP scopes and DNS records in one place to prevent addressing conflicts?
questions.explanation: IP address management tools centralize the planning and tracking of IP space, DHCP and DNS.

questions.prompt: A switch's running configuration no longer matches the approved standard template. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Configuration drift is unmanaged divergence from a golden configuration, often found by automated compliance checks.

questions.prompt: Which document gives detailed, step-by-step instructions for a routine task such as adding a new switch?
questions.explanation: An SOP documents repeatable procedures so tasks are done the same way every time.

questions.prompt: Which document defines what employees may and may not do with company network resources?
questions.explanation: An AUP sets the rules for permitted use of organizational systems and networks.

questions.prompt: In NTP, what does a stratum 1 server get its time from?
choices: Another stratum 1 server over the internet
A directly attached reference clock such as GPS or an atomic clock
questions.explanation: Stratum 0 devices are reference clocks; stratum 1 servers are directly connected to them.

questions.prompt: Financial trading systems need clock synchronization accurate to well under a microsecond. Which protocol is designed for this?
questions.explanation: PTP uses hardware timestamping to reach sub-microsecond accuracy, beyond what NTP typically achieves.

questions.prompt: Administrators must still reach routers through their console ports during a WAN outage. What should be implemented?
choices: Out-of-band management through a console server on a separate connection
In-band SSH over the production WAN
questions.explanation: Out-of-band management uses a separate path so devices stay reachable when production links fail.

questions.prompt: Admins must first connect to a hardened, monitored server before they can reach management interfaces in a secure zone. What is this server called?
questions.explanation: A jump box (jump host) is a controlled entry point for administrative access into a protected network segment.

questions.prompt: A team stores switch configurations as code in Git and pushes them with automation tools. What is a key benefit?
choices: Changes are version-controlled, repeatable and easy to roll back
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as code gives version history, peer review and consistent, automated deployments.

questions.prompt: An NMS is set to alert when a WAN link stays above 85% utilization for 10 minutes. What is this an example of?
questions.explanation: Threshold alerts notify staff when a monitored metric crosses a defined limit for a set time.

questions.prompt: Which neighbor discovery protocol is vendor-neutral and helps map which devices connect to which switch ports?
questions.explanation: LLDP (IEEE 802.1AB) is the open-standard protocol devices use to advertise their identity and capabilities to neighbors.

questions.prompt: Before retiring and selling old firewalls, what should be done?
choices: Disable SNMP but keep everything else
Leave configurations in place so the buyer can reuse them
Wipe configurations and stored data so credentials and keys are removed
questions.explanation: Decommissioning should sanitize devices so passwords, keys and network details are not exposed.

questions.prompt: Two departments agree informally on how they will share a server room, without a binding contract. Which document fits?
questions.explanation: An MOU records shared intentions and responsibilities without the formal penalties of a contract.

questions.prompt: Why do organizations place their DR site in a different geographic region from the primary data center?
choices: To lower latency for every user
So one regional disaster cannot take out both sites
questions.explanation: Geographic diversity keeps a single event such as a flood or regional power failure from affecting both sites.

questions.prompt: Which tool provides graphs of interface usage over time by regularly polling devices with SNMP?
questions.explanation: An NMS polls SNMP counters on a schedule and shows trends, dashboards and alerts.

questions.prompt: Telemetry from routers is pushed continuously to a collector instead of being polled every five minutes. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Streaming telemetry pushes near-real-time data from devices, giving finer detail than periodic polling.

questions.prompt: Why should switches and routers send logs to a central syslog server rather than only keeping them locally?
choices: Local logging is not supported on network devices
Syslog only works when sent to a remote server
Local buffers are small, cleared on reboot, and harder to correlate across devices
Central logging removes the need for timestamps
questions.explanation: Central logging keeps logs after reboots, allows correlation and supports retention requirements.

questions.prompt: Which practice ensures that devices are running vendor-recommended, secure firmware versions?
questions.explanation: Scheduled patch and firmware management closes known vulnerabilities and fixes bugs.

questions.prompt: Which UPS capability most directly protects network equipment during a short utility power loss?
choices: Converting AC power to fiber signals
Battery runtime that bridges the gap until power returns or a generator starts
questions.explanation: A UPS supplies battery power immediately so equipment keeps running through short outages or until a generator takes over.

questions.prompt: An attacker sends forged ARP replies so traffic for the default gateway passes through their laptop. Which switch feature mitigates this?
questions.explanation: DAI checks ARP packets against trusted DHCP snooping bindings and drops forged replies.

questions.prompt: A user plugs a home router into the office network and clients begin receiving wrong gateway addresses. Which feature would have prevented this?
questions.explanation: DHCP snooping allows server responses only from trusted ports, blocking rogue DHCP servers.

questions.prompt: Which feature shuts down an access port if it receives a spanning-tree BPDU?
questions.explanation: BPDU guard err-disables edge ports that receive BPDUs, stopping rogue switches from affecting STP.

questions.prompt: An attacker sends frames with two 802.1Q tags so they reach a VLAN they should not access. How is this best mitigated?
choices: Use VLAN 1 for all user traffic
Set the trunk's native VLAN to an unused VLAN and tag it
questions.explanation: Double-tagging abuses the native VLAN, so moving it to an unused, tagged VLAN defeats the attack.

questions.prompt: An attacker sets up an access point broadcasting the corporate SSID at a stronger signal to capture users' logins. What is this attack?
questions.explanation: An evil twin imitates a legitimate AP to lure clients into connecting through the attacker.

questions.prompt: Users are repeatedly kicked off Wi-Fi by forged management frames sent by an attacker. Which attack is this, and what helps prevent it?
questions.explanation: Forged deauth frames disconnect clients; 802.11w (required in WPA3) protects management frames.

questions.prompt: Users typing a bank's correct URL are sent to a fake site because a resolver cached a forged record. What attack is this?
questions.explanation: DNS poisoning inserts false records into a resolver's cache, sending users to attacker-controlled addresses.

questions.prompt: An attacker sends small, spoofed queries to open DNS resolvers, which send much larger responses to the victim. What is this?
questions.explanation: Amplification attacks use spoofed sources so third-party servers flood the victim with large responses.

questions.prompt: Someone follows an employee through a badge-controlled door without scanning their own badge. What is this?
questions.explanation: Tailgating (piggybacking) is getting physical access by following an authorized person through a secured entrance.

questions.prompt: In 802.1X port-based authentication, what role does the switch play?
questions.explanation: The switch or AP is the authenticator, relaying EAP between the supplicant (client) and the RADIUS server.

questions.prompt: Why might an organization choose TACACS+ over RADIUS for device administration?
choices: TACACS+ encrypts the whole payload and separates authentication, authorization and accounting
TACACS+ uses UDP for faster delivery
TACACS+ is the only protocol that supports 802.1X
questions.explanation: TACACS+ runs over TCP 49, encrypts the full body and allows per-command authorization.

questions.prompt: Which EAP method requires certificates on both the client and the authentication server?
questions.explanation: EAP-TLS uses mutual certificate authentication, which makes it one of the strongest EAP methods.

questions.prompt: WPA3-Personal replaces the WPA2 pre-shared key handshake with which method to resist offline dictionary attacks?
questions.explanation: SAE (Dragonfly) protects against offline password guessing and provides forward secrecy.

questions.prompt: A help desk technician is given only the permissions needed to reset passwords and nothing more. Which principle is this?
questions.explanation: Least privilege gives users only the access their job requires, which limits damage from misuse or compromise.

questions.prompt: A user logs in with a password and then a fingerprint scan. Which factor does the fingerprint represent?
questions.explanation: Biometrics such as fingerprints are inherence factors, or 'something you are'.

questions.prompt: A decoy server with fake data is placed on the network to attract and study attackers. What is it called?
questions.explanation: A honeypot attracts attackers so their methods can be observed without risk to real assets.

questions.prompt: Public-facing web and mail servers are placed in a segment between the internet and the internal LAN. What is this segment called?
questions.explanation: A screened subnet isolates internet-facing services so a compromise does not directly expose the internal network.

questions.prompt: Which firewall capability can block a specific application such as a file-sharing service even when it uses TCP 443?
choices: Application awareness in a next-generation firewall
questions.explanation: NGFWs inspect traffic at Layer 7 to identify applications regardless of the port they use.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between an IDS and an IPS?
choices: An IDS encrypts traffic, while an IPS decrypts it
An IPS only works on wireless networks
An IPS sits inline and can block traffic, while an IDS only monitors and alerts
An IDS must be installed on every host
questions.explanation: An IPS is inline and can drop malicious packets; an IDS usually watches a copy of traffic and raises alerts.

questions.prompt: Which IPsec protocol provides confidentiality by encrypting the payload?
questions.explanation: Encapsulating Security Payload encrypts data; AH provides only integrity and authentication.

questions.prompt: A site-to-site IPsec VPN passes through a NAT device. Which port carries the encapsulated traffic after NAT traversal is detected?
questions.explanation: IKE starts on UDP 500, and NAT-T moves IKE and ESP traffic to UDP 4500 so it can pass through NAT.

questions.prompt: A client must check whether a server's certificate has been revoked, in real time, without downloading a full list. Which mechanism does this?
questions.explanation: The Online Certificate Status Protocol returns the revocation status of a single certificate on request.

questions.prompt: A company puts smart thermostats and cameras on their own VLAN with restrictive ACLs. What is the main security goal?
choices: Avoiding the need for firmware updates
Segmentation to limit damage if an IoT device is compromised
questions.explanation: Segmenting IoT devices keeps a compromised device from reaching sensitive systems.

questions.prompt: Before a laptop gets full network access, its antivirus status and patch level are checked. What NAC function is this?
questions.explanation: Posture assessment checks endpoint health against policy before access is granted or the device is quarantined.

questions.prompt: A secure entry area has two doors, and the second opens only after the first closes and the person is verified. What is it called?
questions.explanation: An access control vestibule (mantrap) lets one person through at a time and prevents tailgating.

questions.prompt: A company processes credit card payments. Which compliance standard governs how cardholder data must be protected?
questions.explanation: The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard sets network and data protection rules for cardholder data.

questions.prompt: Employees sign in once to a corporate identity provider and then reach several cloud apps without logging in again. Which XML-based standard often enables this?
questions.explanation: SAML passes signed authentication assertions from an identity provider to service providers for single sign-on.

questions.prompt: A firewall's last rule drops any traffic that earlier rules did not permit. What concept is this?
questions.explanation: Implicit deny blocks everything not explicitly allowed, a basic part of secure ACL design.

questions.prompt: Following the CompTIA troubleshooting methodology, what should a technician do first?
choices: Identify the problem by gathering information and questioning users
Establish a theory of probable cause
questions.explanation: The first step is identifying the problem: gather information, question users, identify symptoms and find out what changed.

questions.prompt: A technician has confirmed the theory of probable cause. What is the next step in the methodology?
choices: Establish a plan of action to resolve the problem and identify potential effects
questions.explanation: After the theory is confirmed, the technician plans the fix and considers its impact before implementing it.

questions.prompt: Testing shows the technician's theory was wrong. What should happen next?
choices: Establish a new theory or escalate
questions.explanation: If a theory is not confirmed, the technician forms a new theory or escalates to someone with more expertise.

questions.prompt: What is the final step of the troubleshooting methodology?
choices: Test the theory to determine the cause
Document findings, actions, outcomes and lessons learned
questions.explanation: Documentation is the last step and builds a knowledge base for future incidents.

questions.prompt: After applying a fix, a technician confirms users can work normally and adds monitoring to catch a recurrence. Which step is this?
choices: Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures
Establish a theory of probable cause
questions.explanation: This step confirms the problem is truly fixed and takes steps to prevent it from happening again.

questions.prompt: Several users report different network issues at the same time. According to best practice, how should they be handled?
choices: Reboot every network device at once
Assume a single root cause and fix it first
questions.explanation: The methodology says to deal with separate problems one at a time to avoid confusing causes.

questions.prompt: Which command-line tool queries a specific DNS server for a domain's MX records on Linux?
questions.explanation: dig sends DNS queries for any record type to a chosen server, for example 'dig @8.8.8.8 example.com MX'.

questions.prompt: A Windows PC keeps going to a website's old IP address after a DNS change. Which command clears the local resolver cache?
questions.explanation: ipconfig /flushdns removes cached DNS entries so the client queries DNS again.

questions.prompt: Which command shows a host's cache of IP-to-MAC address mappings?
questions.explanation: arp -a lists the ARP table of resolved IPv4 addresses and their MAC addresses.

questions.prompt: Which Linux command lists listening sockets and the processes that own them?
questions.explanation: ss with -t, -u, -l, -p and -n shows TCP/UDP listening sockets with their process IDs, replacing older netstat usage.

questions.prompt: An engineer needs to capture packets on a remote Linux server's interface from the command line and save them for later analysis. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: tcpdump captures packets on the command line and can write pcap files for later analysis in Wireshark.

questions.prompt: Which tool would a technician use to find which TCP ports are open on a server?
questions.explanation: nmap scans hosts to discover open ports, running services and sometimes the operating system.

questions.prompt: Which Windows tool combines traceroute with per-hop packet-loss statistics collected over time?
questions.explanation: pathping traces the route and then sends repeated probes to each hop to measure loss and latency.

questions.prompt: A technician wants to measure the actual maximum TCP throughput between two hosts across a WAN link. Which tool should be used?
questions.explanation: iperf creates test traffic between a client and a server to measure achievable bandwidth.

questions.prompt: Which tool shows the distance in meters to a break in a copper cable?
questions.explanation: A TDR sends a pulse down the cable and times the reflection to locate faults.

questions.prompt: A long fiber run between buildings has high loss, and the technician needs to find where a bad splice is. Which tool is needed?
questions.explanation: An optical time-domain reflectometer measures reflections along fiber to locate splices, bends and breaks.

questions.prompt: Which tool confirms that a newly installed cable run meets Cat6a performance requirements across all parameters?
questions.explanation: A certifier tests against category standards, checking items such as NEXT, insertion loss and return loss.

questions.prompt: Users complain of slow Wi-Fi, and a technician suspects neighboring networks on the same channels. Which tool should be used first?
questions.explanation: A Wi-Fi analyzer shows nearby SSIDs, channels and signal strength, revealing channel overlap.

questions.prompt: A switch interface shows rising late collisions. What is the most likely cause?
choices: A duplex mismatch between the switch and the connected device
questions.explanation: Late collisions usually happen when one side runs half duplex and the other full duplex.

questions.prompt: A switch port has a high count of CRC errors. Which cause should be investigated first?
choices: Too many VLANs on the trunk
A damaged cable or interference on the physical link
An incorrect default gateway on the client
questions.explanation: CRC errors mean frames are corrupted in transit, usually from bad cabling, EMI or failing hardware.

questions.prompt: Interface counters show many frames smaller than 64 bytes. What are these frames called?
questions.explanation: Runts are frames below the 64-byte Ethernet minimum, often caused by collisions or faulty NICs.

questions.prompt: A Windows client shows an IP address of 169.254.12.4 and cannot reach anything off its subnet. What is the most likely problem?
choices: The default gateway is set to the wrong address
The client has a duplicate MAC address
The client cannot reach a DHCP server
questions.explanation: An APIPA address means DHCP failed; check the DHCP service, scope, relay or link connectivity.

questions.prompt: A user can reach 142.250.80.46 by IP address but not by its hostname. Which service is most likely failing?
questions.explanation: If IP connectivity works but names do not resolve, the problem lies with name resolution.

questions.prompt: A host can ping devices on its own subnet but nothing on other subnets. What is the most likely misconfiguration?
questions.explanation: Traffic to remote networks must go to the default gateway, so a bad gateway setting isolates the host to its subnet.

questions.prompt: A host is configured as 192.168.1.130/25 with a default gateway of 192.168.1.1. Why can't it reach other networks?
choices: A /25 mask is invalid for a private network
The gateway is in a different subnet (192.168.1.0/25) from the host (192.168.1.128/25)
The gateway must always be the last usable address
questions.explanation: With a /25, .130 belongs to the .128–.255 subnet, while .1 is in .0–.127, so the gateway is not on-link.

questions.prompt: Two hosts drop connections intermittently, and the event log shows an address conflict. What is the most likely cause?
choices: A duplicate IP address on the network
questions.explanation: When two devices share an IP, ARP caches keep flipping between their MACs, causing intermittent outages.

questions.prompt: After someone connects a cable between two wall jacks on the same switch, the network slows to a crawl and switch CPUs spike. What is happening?
choices: A switching loop causing a broadcast storm
questions.explanation: A Layer 2 loop without STP protection makes broadcasts circulate endlessly and floods the network.

questions.prompt: A traceroute shows the same two router hops repeating until the TTL runs out. What is the problem?
questions.explanation: Repeating hops mean two routers keep forwarding the packet to each other because of incorrect routes.

questions.prompt: Outbound traffic leaves through firewall A, but return traffic comes back through firewall B and is dropped. What is this problem?
questions.explanation: Stateful firewalls drop return packets for sessions they never saw start, which happens with asymmetric paths.

questions.prompt: Wireless users in a break room lose connectivity whenever the microwave is running. What is the most likely cause, and what helps?
choices: Interference in the 2.4 GHz band; move clients to 5 GHz
DNS failure; change the DNS server
Wrong VLAN; retag the AP port
questions.explanation: Microwave ovens give off energy around 2.4 GHz, interfering with Wi-Fi on that band.

questions.prompt: A client's signal strength reads -85 dBm and throughput is very poor. What is the most likely issue?
choices: The signal is too weak; the client is too far from the AP or blocked by obstacles
The signal is too strong and is saturating the radio
questions.explanation: -85 dBm is a weak signal; around -67 dBm or better is usually recommended for reliable data and voice.

questions.prompt: A laptop stays connected to a distant AP with a weak signal even though a closer AP on the same SSID is available. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Sticky clients do not roam to a better AP on their own; tuning minimum RSSI or 802.11k/v/r can help.

questions.prompt: Two neighboring APs on channel 6 hear each other and must take turns transmitting, lowering throughput. What is this?
questions.explanation: APs on the same channel share airtime, so too many in range reduces performance for everyone.

questions.prompt: A new user's laptop sees the corporate SSID but fails to connect with an authentication error, while other users are fine. What should be checked first?
choices: Whether the user entered the right passphrase or credentials
Whether the WAN circuit is down
Whether the core switch's STP priority changed
Whether the AP's PoE budget is exceeded
questions.explanation: When only one client fails authentication, credentials or that client's security settings are the most likely cause.

questions.prompt: A newly patched fiber link shows high loss right after a technician handled the connectors. What should be done first?
choices: Inspect and clean the fiber connector end faces
questions.explanation: Dust and oils on fiber end faces cause major loss, so inspecting and cleaning is the first step.

questions.prompt: A new duplex fiber patch cable gives no link at either end, though both transceivers are fine. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The transmit and receive strands are reversed
The switch ports are in the wrong VLAN
questions.explanation: Each transmitter must connect to the far-end receiver; swapped TX/RX strands prevent link.

questions.prompt: A link stays down between a 10GBASE-SR transceiver and a 10GBASE-LR transceiver. What is the cause?
choices: Mismatched transceiver types (wavelength and fiber mode)
questions.explanation: SR (850 nm, multimode) and LR (1310 nm, single-mode) optics cannot communicate with each other.

questions.prompt: After 10 new IP phones are plugged in, the last few will not power on, though the ports work for laptops. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The phones have duplicate IP addresses
Spanning tree is blocking the ports
The switch's total PoE power budget is exceeded
The voice VLAN is missing from DNS
questions.explanation: Each PoE switch has a total power budget, and devices beyond it are not powered.

questions.prompt: On a busy day, new guests cannot get IP addresses, while devices already connected work fine. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: When all leases in a scope are used, new clients get no address; shorter leases or a larger scope help.

questions.prompt: Small pings to a remote site succeed, but large file transfers and some websites hang. Pinging with the don't-fragment bit at 1472 bytes fails. What is the likely issue?
choices: An incorrect subnet mask on the client
An MTU mismatch along the path
questions.explanation: If large packets with DF set are dropped and ICMP feedback is blocked, a smaller MTU on the path black-holes them.

questions.prompt: A user moves their PC to a new desk, and the switch port goes into an err-disabled state with a security violation. What is the likely cause?
choices: Port security on that port only allows the previous device's MAC address
The PC's DNS cache is full
The port is in the native VLAN
The PC needs a new IPv6 link-local address
questions.explanation: Port security err-disables a port when a MAC address not on its allowed list appears.

questions.prompt: A printer gets an address from the wrong subnet after being moved to a different jack. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The new switch port is assigned to a different VLAN
questions.explanation: Each access port belongs to a VLAN, so a port in the wrong VLAN puts the device in a different subnet.

questions.prompt: A switch logs CDP or LLDP warnings about a native VLAN mismatch on a trunk. What is the effect?
choices: Untagged traffic leaks between different VLANs on each side
The trunk automatically renegotiates the speed
questions.explanation: When native VLANs differ, untagged frames from one VLAN are put into a different VLAN on the other switch.

questions.prompt: Users get browser warnings when visiting an internal web portal that worked yesterday, and nothing on the server changed. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The server's TLS certificate has expired
questions.explanation: An expired certificate makes browsers show trust warnings even though the server is reachable.

questions.prompt: Domain users suddenly fail Kerberos authentication, and the domain controller's clock is 12 minutes off. What should be fixed?
choices: Time synchronization (NTP) on the domain controller and clients
questions.explanation: Kerberos rejects tickets when clock skew is more than about five minutes by default, so NTP must be correct.

questions.prompt: Unshielded cables running beside large electric motors on a factory floor show heavy errors. What is the best fix?
choices: Reroute the cables away from the motors or use shielded cabling
questions.explanation: EMI from motors corrupts signals on UTP; distance or shielding (STP) reduces it.

questions.prompt: A traceroute shows asterisks at one hop, but later hops reply and the destination is reached. What is the best conclusion?
choices: There is a routing loop at that hop
That router is likely rate-limiting or ignoring ICMP/TTL-exceeded messages, not dropping traffic
questions.explanation: Since later hops answer and the destination is reached, the silent hop is just not replying to traceroute probes.

questions.prompt: After a new ACL is applied, users can no longer reach a server, and the ACL only contains permit statements for other hosts. Why?
choices: The ACL's implicit deny at the end blocks traffic that was not permitted
ACLs always block servers by default regardless of rules
Permit statements also block their own traffic
questions.explanation: Anything not matched by a permit statement is dropped by the implicit deny at the end of the ACL.
